citation.title: Corporate Capture of the IMO
citation.type: web landing page summarising a report

question: How the shipping industry has lobbied the UN (International Maritime Organization) to obstruct climate action for shipping.

findings.claim: At the most recent IMO environmental committee meeting, 31% of nations were represented in part by direct business interests (industry representatives inside national delegations). Which meeting, the count, the denominator and the source list are not stated on the page.
findings.quote: at the most recent IMO environmental committee meeting 31% of nations were represented in part by direct business interests

findings.claim: The authors state that the IMO is the only UN agency to allow such extensive corporate representation. This is the authors' claim; the page gives no comparison data.
findings.quote: The IMO appears to be the only UN agency to allow such extensive corporate representation in the policy-making process.

findings.claim: Shipping trade associations (ICS, BIMCO, World Shipping Council) are reported to have lobbied to delay climate regulation until 2023 and to support only voluntary measures.
findings.quote: collectively lobbied to delay implementation of any climate regulations until 2023

limitations.point: This is a summary web page, not the full report. The full report and graphic are behind a registration or login download, and were not read.
limitations.quote: You will be required to register or login to our site to download these files.

limitations.point: The page does not say how the 31% was measured: no data source, meeting, number of delegations, definition of 'direct business interests', or classification rule is given. It cannot be compared with a count from UNFCCC participant lists without the full report.

The 31% is a share of nations with at least some business representation ('in part'), not a share of delegation members. It is also not specific to fossil-fuel industries (it covers shipping and related business).
limitations.quote: 31% of nations were represented in part by direct business interests

limitations.point: The page is a campaign-style summary and mixes findings with advocacy and recommendations (for example, that investors should question shipping companies). Only the findings above are recorded as findings.
Publication date is taken from the section heading '2017-10-01'; the page metadata gives no published or modified date.
